reduced mouth opening
two prior similar episodes over eight years
no pain or fever
a known diabetic on regular medication

concepts.why: The patient has a two-week history of an asymptomatic swelling in the right lower half of the face, with a previous similar episode treated as a buccal-space infection, and the CT scan shows a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas in the right buccal space.
The patient is a known diabetic and has a gross right facial asymmetry with a subcutaneous swelling, which could be related to diabetic cheilitis.
The CT scan shows a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas in the right buccal space, which could be a buccal space cyst.
The patient has a history of a similar episode treated as a buccal-space infection, and the current episode could be a staphylococcal abscess.
The patient has a history of a similar episode treated as a buccal-space infection, and the current episode could be an actinomycotic abscess.

The patient has a gross right facial asymmetry with a subcutaneous swelling, and the CT scan shows a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas in the right buccal space, which could be a sign of necrotizing fasciitis.

rationales.F01: Asymptomatic swelling in the right lower half of the face is consistent with a chronic buccal space abscess.
rationales.F02: Reduced mouth opening is a common symptom of a chronic buccal space abscess.
rationales.F10: Contrast-enhanced CT showing a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas in the right buccal space is highly suggestive of a chronic buccal space abscess.
rationales.F11: Intracystic loculations with dense cystic content and erosion of the posterior buccal cortex without perforation of the maxilla are characteristic of a chronic buccal space abscess.
rationales.F12: A clinical diagnosis of a nonspecific chronic abscess with buccal-space involvement strongly supports the diagnosis of a chronic buccal space abscess.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of recurrent asymptomatic swellings, the presence of a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas in the right buccal space on CT, and the clinical findings of a firm, irregular, leathery pouch-like appearance of the excised specimen support this diagnosis.
